P0: Accounts, keys and folders that everything else needs, kept safe: password manager, the YouTube API key, the channel and Instagram account, one private repo, and a secrets file outside git.
P1: Measure what works before building: compare six topic lanes, study the Shorts that broke out from small channels, and turn the numbers into a quality bar every video must pass.
P2: A clear, natural voice made locally for free: install Kokoro, pick the house voice by ear, and turn script lines into audio clips of known length at the right loudness.
P3: A library of polished, reusable animation templates, so each video only fills in data: choose the renderer, define the scene-plan format, lock the look, then build the templates.
P4: Fresh ideas collected from news and trend sources, ranked by one cheap AI call, then turned into a script and scene plan where every fact has a source.
P5: Footage, images, music and sound effects that may legally be used on a channel that could earn money, with a licence record for each one.
P6: One command builds the finished video; automatic checks and an AI review test it against the quality bar; nothing goes out without Talha's approval.
P7: Ready-to-paste titles, descriptions and captions for manual upload, then statistics after 48 hours and a weekly report on what to change.
P8: Three pilot videos in three lanes, a week of daily posting, and a retrospective that adjusts the lane mix with real numbers.
P9: Quality v2: a human-style scriptwriter with a named narrator (Habit), a director that storyboards drawn, fast-cut scenes, an expressive voice, a sound-design layer and a stricter quality bar, proven on a Black October pilot video.
P10: One video a day on its own, with Talha deciding on Telegram: a 14:00 topic card, a 15:00 auto-pick, the make, a video card to approve, and posting at 11:30 on YouTube, Instagram and Facebook.
P11: Every video teaches the next: reviews, Talha's notes and 48-hour stats become lessons the writer and director read, and the ones that keep helping become house rules.
P12: Spend less per video: reuse drawings and clips that worked, clean up old renders, and turn the same research into a Habit card post.
P13: The public side: a read-only Studio web app with every run and video, and a betadoc story page with a narrated tour, both deployed by git push.
P14: One local control panel to watch and steer every step, with the same buttons as Telegram and a live view of what a make is doing.
P15: Work like a real studio: each role is a desk with its own check, fixes happen on a cheap draft (the animatic), and the real render happens once.
P16: Make the studio visible: a pixel-art production house where every desk of the board is a person at work. From the street you see every floor; tap one to go inside, watch the last make climb the building, and open any desk's card for what it did.
P24: Turn the daily Short into a show: Habit at a news desk, seen in four framings (the full studio, a close-up in the bottom third blended into the visuals, a square window at the bottom left, and visuals alone). Scripts are told as one story, 75-90 s. Samples come first; Talha picks the set, Habit's look, the intro and the topics before anything changes in the daily make.
